title: How the Room Rate of a Resort Lodging Stay Is Worked Out
content:
The room rate for a Resort Lodging stay is worked out night by night and posted to the folio as a single entry covering every night of the stay.

**The nights.** A night falling inside the published holiday window of the unit type is priced at its holiday nightly rate, a night falling inside its published peak window at its peak nightly rate, and every other night at its base nightly rate, and those nightly amounts are added together to give the room rate for the stay before any reduction.

**The order in which the reductions are taken.** The passholder reduction is taken first, on the room rate for the stay before any reduction. The advance booking reduction is taken next, on the amount left after the passholder reduction. The length-of-stay reduction is taken third, on the amount left after the advance booking reduction. The package reduction is taken last, on the amount left after the length-of-stay reduction. Each of the four acts on the amount the one before it left, and never on the room rate before any reduction a second time.

**The occupancy charge.** Each guest beyond the unit type's standard occupancy is charged at the unit type's extra person nightly charge for every night of the stay, so the occupancy charge is that nightly charge multiplied by the number of guests beyond the standard occupancy and multiplied by the nights of the stay. That occupancy charge is added only after every reduction has been taken, because reductions are given on the room rate and never on the occupancy charge.

**Precision.** The amounts are carried at full precision through every step and the entry posted to the folio is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end. An amount that falls exactly halfway between two cents is rounded to the cent whose last digit is even, which is the convention the collective's finance office settles every folio on.

### A worked stay (hypothetical figures throughout)

Take a stay of 4 nights, every night of it outside both published windows, in a unit type whose base nightly rate is taken here as 300.00 USD, whose standard occupancy is taken as 2 and whose extra person nightly charge is taken as 40.00 USD, for a party of 4 guests.

Each of the 4 nights is priced at 300.00 USD, and adding those nightly amounts together gives 1200.00 USD as the room rate for the stay before any reduction. The four reductions are then taken on that amount in their order, each on what the one before it left.

The party carries 2 guests beyond the standard occupancy of 2, so the occupancy charge is 40.00 USD multiplied by 2 guests and multiplied by 4 nights, which is 320.00 USD. That 320.00 USD is added to the amount the reductions leave, and the total is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end, to give the amount of the entry.
